review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an argue that in school, only students with the best academic results should be rewarded, while their counterparts prefer to reward improving student. From my perspective, both types of learners should receive their own encouraging gift.

Admittedly, rewarding best individuals without any arguments is a must do thing. Initially, students who had diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, which leads to propelling towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition could be seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students are adapted this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which allows them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show improvements should also be rewarded. Only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, causing others to think that their effort is futile since they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. Which will prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. In addition, emphasizing improvements will encourage all students to be diligent in their studies, and helps students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, which irrespective of how well they have been or are performing, leads to the constant desire to outdo themselves that even benefit themselves more than competitive determination against others.
review.overall: Em đã triển khai đủ hai quan điểm và giữ được bốn chuỗi ý Cô giao, từ nỗ lực được ghi nhận đến giá trị của việc vượt chính mình. Em dùng đúng nhiều cụm của buổi học, nhưng câu thường thiếu động từ chính hoặc sai cấu trúc sau động từ nên quan hệ giữa các ý chưa rõ. Em cũng chưa viết kết bài trên trang này; bản sửa bổ sung để khẳng định lập trường thưởng cả hai nhóm. Trước khi nộp, hãy kiểm tra từng câu có chủ ngữ, động từ chính và đối tượng quy chiếu rõ hay chưa.

Admittedly, one might argue, dangerous sports should be forbidden since even a minor error can lead to the death of a participant obviously in sky diving. However, this idea is not possible due to several condition. Initially, most of the extreme sports takes place in remote locations, say, mountain cliffs having minimal surveillance and control. That means a prohibition existed only on paper can make there dangerous practice driving underground which is a lot harder to ensure basic safety standard.

To add more evidencesto my opinion, I think that people should have the permission to do any sport, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. Some activities as deep-ocean diving and bungee jumping often need a reputable club having appropriate and qualified supervision. With an expert, It's crucial to be accompanied by an expert, who will teach survival knowledge when accidents occur. This will help participants recognise danger and respond appropriately. Due to the proper training and necessary precautions, there will be safer participations since no activities is entirely risk-free.

paragraphs: There is an argument about whether dangerous sports should be banned by law or every individual should be free to take part in these activities. I am personally of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be forbidden since even a minor error can lead to a participant's death, as in skydiving. However, I do not think a ban is possible in practice, for several reasons. Initially, most extreme sports take place in remote locations, such as mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. It is also unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow every individual personally. This means that a prohibition may exist only on paper and may drive dangerous sports underground, making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To support my opinion, I think people should be permitted to do any sport as long as they understand the risks and receive sufficient training. People who try deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should join a reputable club with appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Beginners should be accompanied by an expert who teaches them what to do when accidents occur. This will help participants recognise danger and respond appropriately. With proper training and necessary precautions, participation will be safer, although no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I think banning extreme sports is neither practical nor effective. Moreover, freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: There is an argue that children should be free to make mistakes, whereas others think that adults should help them avoid mistakes. Personally, I believe that the freedom to make mistakes should be encouraged, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of trial-and-error approach emphasise that most mistakes can be avoidable, for instance, knives, fire and electricity which is unnecessary to get hurt to be careful. Moreover, parents take responsibility to shield their children from harm, means that they need to forestall mistakes to fulfil this duty. By pre-emptively helping children, adults will have peace of mind since they did their best to protect and raised their child.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasoning. Initially, It is unrealistic for adults to prevent all the mistakes as they cannot be around their children all the time, so that their experiments with new things and making mistakes is inevitable. Furthermore, these mistakes can bring invaluable lessons to their children that plays an important role to stand them in good stead in later stages of life. Lastly, the younger generation shielded from every thing will grow up overdependent on others.

It seems to me that allowing children from mistakes is preparing for the future, provided that parents should intervene and give guidance on importance matters so that they can prevent errors that may derail children's future

task.text:
WRITING TASK 1
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.
The graph below shows the three different kinds of emission sources (oil/coal/gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK.
Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
Write at least 150 words.

images.alt: Biểu đồ khí thải từ oil, coal và gas tại Anh, 1990–2010

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates the amount of three different types of emission sources of green house gas in the UK over a 20 years period, comencing from 1990.
Overall, there is a general fall in the amount of emission by Oil and coal whereas the figures for gas witnesses a noticeable increase in the same amount of time.

To elaborate, starting at about 220 million tons in 1990, the amount of carbon emissions from Gas went up reaching 270 million in 1995. The figures for oil and Coal, conversely, observed a decrease from 270 and 310 million tons in 1990 to 240 and 280 million tons in 1995.

Regarding the latter time of the period, the amount of gas emissions continued to increase consistently till the end of the study, reaching 320 million tons. This number marking the peak of entire chart. The figure for oil unexpectedly arise to 260 millions ton in 2000 before a slightly fall in the rest with 240 million in 2005 and 210 million in 2010. The figure for coal continuously decrease to reach 190 million in 2010.
review.overall: Cô thấy em đã ghi được ba hướng thay đổi chính và nhắc tới việc oil tăng lại vào năm 2000. Em cần thêm vào overview sự đổi ngôi: coal cao nhất năm đầu, gas cao nhất từ 2000. Trong phần chi tiết, hãy bỏ từ cảm xúc “unexpectedly”, ghi đơn vị nhất quán là “million tons” và sửa các câu thiếu động từ chia thì, nhất là câu về mức đỉnh.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows carbon emissions from gas, oil and coal in the United Kingdom at five points between 1990 and 2010. Figures are given in millions of tons.

Overall, emissions from gas increased and became the highest of the three by 2000. By contrast, those from coal declined throughout the period. Oil ended below its starting level, despite a temporary rise from 1995 to 2000. Coal was the largest source at the beginning, while gas led at the end.

In 1990, gas accounted for around 220 million tons of emissions, compared with approximately 270 million tons from oil and 310 million tons from coal. By 1995, gas had risen to roughly 270 million tons, whereas oil and coal had fallen to about 240 and 280 million tons respectively. Five years later, gas reached 300 million tons and overtook the other fuels. Oil recovered to around 260 million tons, while coal continued to fall to approximately 250 million tons.

From 2000 to 2010, gas emissions increased more slowly, reaching about 320 million tons, the highest figure on the chart. Oil emissions declined from roughly 260 to 210 million tons over these ten years. Coal followed a similar downward path, decreasing from around 250 to 190 million tons by 2010.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: There is an argue that history is the most important school subjects, while others think that history is not as crucial as science and technology. From my perspective, I am the latter school of thought.

Admittedly, history brings us unreplaceable advantages. Learning history is not only about events in the past, but also the knowledge and the experiences. Which is important for everyone in latter life. Personally, I think its advantages is less noticeable as science and technology in today life.
However, This is the technology era
review.overall: Cô thấy em đã nêu rõ mình nghiêng về khoa học và công nghệ, đồng thời nhận ra lịch sử có ích. Bài dừng ngay khi em mở luận điểm thứ hai, nên người đọc chưa thấy lý do vì sao em chọn phía đó hoặc ví dụ để kiểm chứng. Ở lần viết sau, em hãy hoàn thành mỗi thân bài theo luận điểm–giải thích–ví dụ và kết bằng một câu nhắc lại ý kiến. Với phần đã viết, cần sửa câu “Which is important...” thành một câu hoàn chỉnh.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.comment: Em nêu được hai phía và chọn phía khoa học, công nghệ, nhưng chỉ giải thích rất ngắn ích lợi lịch sử; phía em ủng hộ mới có câu mở chưa phát triển.

criteria.label: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.comment: Có mở bài, đoạn nhượng bộ và mở đoạn tiếp; bài dừng trước luận cứ, ví dụ và kết luận nên lập luận chưa thành chuỗi.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.comment: Một số từ chủ đề phù hợp như “history”, “science and technology”, “experiences”; nhiều kết hợp từ chưa chính xác.

criteria.label: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.comment: Câu đơn và một số cấu trúc so sánh có mặt, nhưng lỗi câu rời, hòa hợp và dạng từ xuất hiện ở hầu hết phần đã viết.

paragraphs.text: Some people regard history as the most important school subject, whereas others place more value on science and technology. I agree with the latter view, although studying history remains valuable.

History gives students knowledge of earlier decisions and their consequences. When young people study past conflicts, for example, they can consider how communities dealt with disagreement and what those choices meant for ordinary people. This can help them understand institutions and cultural traditions in the society where they live. Historical study also encourages them to compare different accounts of the same event instead of accepting a single version without question. These benefits are relevant to civic life, even if they are less visible than some technical skills.

Science and technology, however, are especially useful in a world where work and daily life are changing rapidly. Science lessons teach pupils to test claims and use evidence, while technology lessons help them apply ideas to practical problems. For instance, students who learn basic programming can create a simple tool to organise information for their class. The process requires planning, testing and correcting mistakes. These abilities may help them enter fields such as healthcare, engineering and digital services, but they also make them more confident users of technology in everyday life. Schools should therefore provide enough time and resources for these subjects.

In conclusion, history helps students interpret the human past, but science and technology offer practical ways to investigate and shape the future. Both belong in schools; nevertheless, I would give science and technology greater priority because their methods and skills are increasingly relevant to students’ lives.
